transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes, is that still good?
[00:05] Ravi Singh: Yeah that's perfect. Thanks Maya.
[00:12] Jordan Patel: Hi team, Jordan from Redwood, I'll be helping on the technical side — quick heads up I'll drop some links in the chat.
[00:20] Elena Morales: Great, thanks. We're mainly here to see how fast we can get up and running, and what the path is if we need dedicated capacity later.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Awesome. So high level: Redwood has a self-serve hosted API you can sign up for, we give free credits for quick experiments, and then Dedicated or Private when you need isolation and predictable throughput. Today's goal: understand your success criteria, timelines, and any blockers.
[00:45] Ravi Singh: Sounds good. For context, we're a four-person infra team supporting ML features across engineering. We're looking to replace a mix of open-source hosting and some calls to a major API provider. Cost is an issue but latency is more important for some endpoints.
[01:05] Jordan Patel: Understood. Can you share current numbers — qps, typical request size, and token lengths?
[01:12] Samir Khan: We're at about 30 qps at peak for embeddings, average 512 tokens for chat-ish features, though the initial pilot would be just a few hundred requests per minute.
[01:25] Jordan Patel: Ok that maps well to our quickstart. Our hosted API should get you to first token in under 5 minutes from signup if you follow the quickstart, with SDKs and curl examples. We also provision sandbox orgs with credits so you can run sample prompts and a small benchmark.
[01:40] Elena Morales: How do credits work? Are they limited to hosted only?
[01:45] Maya Chen: Free credits are for hosted API use to validate functionality and perf. If you decide to go Dedicated later, we'll apply credits toward setup or pilot fees — we can walk through that.
[01:55] Ravi Singh: Ok. On the Dedicated vs Private side: we may need VPC peering or customer-managed VPC eventually. Also encryption keys — we have to use our KMS.
[02:05] Jordan Patel: We support VPC and Private deployments. For KMS we integrate with common cloud KMS providers; we also offer HSM options for Private installs. For hosted, you can bring-your-own-key in some enterprise plans, otherwise keys are managed.
[02:20] Samir Khan: Any audit log support? We need traceability for queries and token usage.
[02:24] Jordan Patel: Yes, Redwood Console exposes request-level logs, token breakdowns, and you can ingest traces into your observability. For Private you get more retention controls.
[02:35] Elena Morales: Latency — do you have benchmarks? We care about 95th percentile under 200 ms for short prompts.
[02:45] Jordan Patel: For short generation with smaller models we commonly hit <200 ms p95 on NVIDIA A10/A100 class hardware; it varies by model family and length. We also do automatic batching and KV cache to optimize throughput. If tight latency is required, Dedicated pools with pinned GPUs and specific kernel selection helps.
[03:10] Ravi Singh: What's the typical time to provision a Dedicated pool?
[03:15] Maya Chen: For standard sizes, provisioning a Dedicated pool is usually a few days for capacity planning and contract; Private/VPC/on-prem takes longer — a few weeks with ops coordination. But for pilots, we recommend Hosted with sandbox credits.
[03:30] Elena Morales: Cool. For the quickstart, what's the exact "time-to-first-token" path — we want to present it internally.
[03:38] Jordan Patel: Step 1: sign up at the console, create an API key; Step 2: run our sample curl or SDK snippet to call the text-generation or embeddings endpoint; Step 3: configure model and temperature. If you follow it, first token can be seconds after you supply the key. The sandbox org we give includes sample prompts, a small dataset for embeddings, and a prepopulated notebook.
[03:58] Ravi Singh: Any notable gotchas? E.g., rate limits, cold starts, or model warm-up times?
[04:05] Jordan Patel: The hosted API has soft rate limits on the free tier; for production you request custom quotas. Cold KV cache or cold model variants can add a small latency spike — we mitigate with warm-up traffic and autoscale policies. Also note that quantized model variants can change output slightly; we surface quality tradeoffs in the Optimize tool.
[04:30] Elena Morales: You mentioned Optimize. Can you explain how that helps cut cost without breaking quality?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize suggests batching configs, caching prefixes, and model/quantization suggestions based on your workload. It also hooks into evals so you can detect regressions. For example for embeddings workload we often recommend a 16-32 batch with prefix caching to reduce per-token cost.
[05:00] Ravi Singh: Security: SSO, SAML, RBAC?
[05:05] Jordan Patel: We support SAML/SSO for orgs, role-based access controls in the Console, and audit logs. For Private, you can connect to your internal identity provider directly.
[05:18] Samir Khan: Are there customers in regulated verticals using hosted?
[05:22] Maya Chen: A number of customers in fintech and health start with hosted for experimentation then move to Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads. We can share redacted SOC2 report and security whitepaper.
[05:35] Elena Morales: Great. On pricing — are we looking at per-token and per-embedding pricing or flat commits?
[05:41] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based (per-token/per-embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits and lower unit price. Private has platform fees plus support. I'll send concrete examples based on your expected qps.
[05:55] Ravi Singh: For our pilot, we'd want to test embeddings and a small chat flow. Would free credits cover that?
[06:00] Maya Chen: Yes, free credits are usually enough for a 2-week pilot. We'll attach a sandbox org and credits.
[06:06] Jordan Patel: I'll add notes on benchmarking scripts — we'd like to run a 5k token sample and a series of 512-token chat requests to measure p95. We can help run remote bench or you can run locally and share the results.
[06:20] Elena Morales: About model catalog — do you support custom model uploads?
[06:25] Jordan Patel: For hosted we serve curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. For Private you can bring your own model artifacts and our runtime will deploy them. There's an onboarding process for model versions and rollouts.
[06:40] Ravi Singh: How does fallback work if capacity is constrained?
[06:44] Jordan Patel: We have smart routing and fallbacks to compatible model variants or other regions; Dedicated customers can configure fallback tiers.
[06:50] Maya Chen: Quick check: what's your timeline?
[06:53] Ravi Singh: We'd like to run a pilot in the next two weeks and decide by end of month if we go Dedicated next quarter.
[07:01] Maya Chen: Good — so immediate focus: send sandbox invite + credits, security docs, and pricing. Also schedule a benchmark session.
[07:10] Elena Morales: One question: does Redwood's Console show per-route token cost?
[07:15] Jordan Patel: Yes, we show token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards and traces.
[07:22] Samir Khan: Any thought on inference cost reduction approaches? We prefer batching but latency-sensitive endpoints make batching harder.
[07:29] Jordan Patel: Right — that's a classic tradeoff. Optimize helps with mixed policies: sync endpoints stay low-latency with smaller batches while asynchronous or background endpoints use larger batches. Also caching prefixes and KV cache reduces compute for repeated contexts.
[07:45] Ravi Singh: If we do a Private on-prem deployment later, what are the requirements?
[07:51] Jordan Patel: For on-prem we need a minimum node footprint depending on model sizes, and you'll need network routing for the control plane or a private control plane option. We provide an installer, and professional services can help.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Ok want to go over the proposed next steps and owners?
[08:09] Ravi Singh: Yes.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Jordan will provision the sandbox and share quickstart steps + sample scripts; I will send pricing and SOC2/security docs; Ravi will confirm latency targets and pilot dataset by 4/14; we will tentatively schedule the benchmark call for the week of 4/20.
[08:25] Elena Morales: That works.
[08:28] Samir Khan: Quick nit — can you include example curl for embeddings with retry logic?
[08:32] Jordan Patel: Yup will include retry example and recommended client-side rate limiting.
[08:36] Ravi Singh: Any closing notes on contract terms for Dedicated?
[08:40] Maya Chen: We can do monthly or annual commits; annual gives better unit price. We'll tailor a sample proposal after we see pilot metrics.
[08:50] Elena Morales: Thanks everyone — looking forward to the sandbox.
[08:53] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:00] -- End of recording --
